title: High Country field season
question: How do you know where you are, and how do you show a route to someone who is not standing beside you?

intro.speaker: Ranger Wren
lines: The crew marked sites. The sketch in your tablet is all they had time to draw.
Survey point is north of here. If you lose the trail, the land will still be there.

completeJournalEntry.title: Field plan
completeJournalEntry.text: The route to the radio site is a choice with tradeoffs, written from coordinates, distance, elevation, and what the image showed that the sketch did not.

idle: Start with a marker. The tablet's first reading will be rough. Walk closer if the numbers feel too round.
afterMarkers: Two trails reach the ridge. We need to move a heavy sampling case. Measure both before you pick.
afterRoutes: Stand on the west cliff, then the east meadow. Toggle the topo layer when you have it. The land should explain the lines.
afterContours: The radio site sits beyond a rise you cannot see from the junction. Guess the shape first. Then cut the profile.
afterProfile: We need a temporary observation pad: near a trail, not in wet ground, not on the cliff, open enough to see sky. No single drawing answers that.
afterGis: The west switchback still looks whole on the sketch. Look at the newer image. Then look at the ground.
afterImagery: The radio site still needs a route a person can defend. Not the shortest line. The one you can walk.
afterSuccess: High Country will still be here. Cedar Hollow too. The tools stay with the tablet.

routes.goal: We need to move a heavy sampling case to the ridge survey. Which trail makes more sense?
routes.stormGoal: A storm may arrive later. Which trail is faster, and what land does it cross?

reasons.label: It is the shorter walk on the map.
The west face would show tight contour spacing.
The meadow would show wide contour spacing.
A heavy case is safer on the gentler trail.
If we only cared about time, the short trail wins.

challenge.title: The route above treeline
challenge.prompt: Plan a field route to the radio site. There is not one correct trail. There is a route you can defend.

routes.label: West switchback
routes.hint: The west trail is shorter on the sketch, but the image and the washout say that line is no longer a trail.

routes.label: East meadow trail
routes.hint: Longer, gentler, and it still exists on the ground.

routes.label: Saddle cut
routes.hint: Not the shortest, not the gentlest — it misses the washout and the cliff band.

reasons.label: It avoids the broken west switchback.
It stays off the cliff band.
It asks for less steep climbing with gear.
It is the shortest line on the sketch.
The profile shows a rise we can actually walk.
It stays out of the wet shore.
